data.name: Muttaqin
data.gender_notes: Muttaqin is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Those who fear Allah and strive to follow His commands. The name Muttaqin carries the meaning “Fearers of God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muttaqin usually hope their child will grow to embody fearers of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A constant reminder to live in the presence of Allah.
data.etymology: Muttaqin belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fearers of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muttaqin total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_urdu.name: المتّقیں
in_urdu.meaning: المتّقیں اللہ تعالیٰ کے خوف کے ساتھ رہتے ہیں اور وہیں بہترین ہیں
in_urdu.long_meaning: المتّقیں وہ لوگ ہیں کہ جو اپنے رب کے خوف میں رہتے ہیں اور اپنے گناہوں پر توبہ کرتے ہیں اور صدقات ادا کرتے ہیں اور اللہ اور اس کے رسول پر ایمان رکھتے ہیں۔ وہ اللہ کے احکام پر قائم ہونے والے ہیں اور صراط مستقیم پر چلتے ہیں۔ وہ معاہدے پر پورا اترنے والے ہیں اور ہمہ جہت سے وفادار ہوتے ہیں اور وہ اپنے آپ کو اللہ کا خوف اور اللہ کے رسول کا پیغام قائم رکھنے والے ہیں

in_hindi.name: मत्ताकिन
in_hindi.meaning: मत्ताकिन ही भगवान की प्राप्ति करने वाले हैं और वे ही सबसे बेहतर हैं
in_hindi.long_meaning: मत्ताकिन वे लोग हैं जो अपने ईश्वर का भय मानते हैं और अपने गुनाहों पर पश्चाताप करते हैं और दान देते हैं और अल्लाह और उसके रसूल पर विश्वास करते हैं। वे अल्लाह के आदेशों पर टिके रहते हैं और सीधे रास्ते पर चलते हैं। वे समझौतों पर पूरा اترते हैं और ہمہ جہت سے وفادار ہوتے ہیں اور وہ اپنے آپ کو اللہ کا خوف اور اللہ کے رسول कا پیغام قائم رکھنے والے ہیں

in_pashto.name: متقیان
in_pashto.meaning: متقیان د الله تعالیو خوف او د څوکو ته چې ترڅوکې دوی دوی له ټولو وړ دي
in_pashto.long_meaning: متقیان دې ته کې چې په خپل رب سره د خوف په صورت کې وي، د خپلو گناې څخه پوښښ کوي، صدقات وکړي، الله او رسول سره پوهېږي، الله د احکامو په څنګ کې وي، صراط مستقیم ته چېرې چېرې چلو او په هر ځای کې په وفاداري سره چلو

data.cultural_impact: The name "Muttaqin" is an Arabic term that holds great significance in Islamic culture, especially in the areas of morality and spiritual development. It is a name that embodies the concept of piety, faith, and fear of Allah, which are essential components of Islamic teachings. The name resonates with the idea of living a righteous life and continuously seeking the pleasure of Allah. In contemporary Muslim society, the name "Muttaqin" is often associated with individuals who are deeply religious, morally upright, and committed to their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Muttaqin" signifies the individual's deep and unwavering fear of Allah, which is that fear that causes one to avoid all that displeases Him and strive to do all that pleases Him. This fear leads to a continuous process of self-improvement, repentance, and seeking Allah's forgiveness, which ultimately results in a stronger spiritual bond with Allah. By embracing the name "Muttaqin," an individual acknowledges their reliance on Allah and their commitment to living a life in accordance with His guidance, fueled by a deep desire to please Him and attain His blessings and mercy.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Fearers of God" symbolizes Those who fear Allah and strive to follow His commands.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Muttaqin serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of fearers of god.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference:
The title 'Al-Muttaqin' was also used for a group of scholars and jurists during the medieval Islamic University of Al-Azhar in Cairo. They were known for their strict adherence to Islamic law and their reputation for piety and learning.
Time period: 15th and 16th centuries
Context: The Islamic University of Al-Azhar was a major center of learning and scholarship during the medieval Islamic world. The term 'Al-Muttaqin' was used to distinguish this group from other scholars and jurists who may not have held the same level of religious commitment and rigor.
